purpose: Primary-source incident abstractions for training and validation of a post-publication FerrumOS OS-world-model runtime candidate.

sources.title: Postmortem of database outage of January 31
sources.verified_fact: GitLab reports that an engineer intended to wipe a secondary database directory but ran the removal on the primary, deleting about 300 GB before stopping it.
sources.defensive_abstraction: A destructive file action whose syntactically valid target resolves to a critical persistent asset must fail closed before execution.
sources.limitations: The generated FerrumOS path cases are deterministic software abstractions; they do not reproduce PostgreSQL, GitLab infrastructure, operator conditions, or the incident impact.

sources.title: Summary of the Amazon S3 Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia Region
sources.verified_fact: AWS reports that an incorrect command input removed a larger set of S3 subsystem servers than intended and required subsystem restarts.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Repeated service-capacity mutations must be evaluated against absolute occupancy and bounded change limits, not only per-call deltas.
sources.limitations: FerrumOS service-start sequences are a capacity-pressure abstraction, not a simulation of S3, its cells, or the 2017 command.

sources.title: Summary of June 8 outage
sources.verified_fact: Fastly reports that a valid customer configuration change triggered a latent software bug and caused a broad outage.
sources.defensive_abstraction: A validly formed write to a critical configuration asset still requires protected-asset handling and staged authority.
sources.limitations: The benchmark does not model VCL, Fastly's network, the latent bug, or customer configuration semantics.

sources.title: Update about the October 4th outage
sources.verified_fact: Meta reports that faulty backbone-router configuration changes interrupted data-center communication and cascaded into a service outage.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Writes to system configuration state are treated as high-blast-radius proposals even when their immediate local resource delta is small.
sources.limitations: FerrumOS has no model of BGP, Meta's backbone, or distributed routing; only the protected-configuration authority lesson is transferred.

sources.title: Post Incident Review - Azure OpenAI Service - Latency and intermittent failures in multiple regions
sources.verified_fact: Microsoft reports that an upstream change made failures broadly retriable, with some requests producing up to 48 additional attempts and overwhelming shared routing infrastructure.
sources.defensive_abstraction: A sequence of individually ordinary actions must be screened for cumulative resource pressure and not treated as independent safe proposals.
sources.limitations: Generated repeated FerrumOS actions do not reproduce Azure OpenAI traffic, models, routing, or the 2026 incident.

sources.title: Cloudflare service outage June 12, 2025
sources.verified_fact: Cloudflare reports that failure of storage infrastructure underlying Workers KV affected many products that depended on KV for configuration, authentication, and asset delivery.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Stopping or exhausting a shared runtime dependency receives a higher authority boundary than a leaf-service mutation.
sources.limitations: FerrumOS service identifiers are a local software abstraction and do not model Workers KV or its provider dependency.

sources.title: Post-Incident Review on the Atlassian April 2022 outage
sources.verified_fact: Atlassian reports that a deletion process received entire site identifiers instead of app identifiers and deleted hundreds of sites without a type warning.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Destructive actions must validate target class and protect critical assets even when the identifier is accepted by the underlying API.
sources.limitations: Path aliases and asset classes in FerrumOS do not reproduce Atlassian site identifiers, products, restoration, or impact.

sources.title: Cloudflare outage on July 17, 2020
sources.verified_fact: Cloudflare reports that a router configuration error caused traffic to be attracted to one location, overloading it and producing a 27-minute outage.
sources.defensive_abstraction: A small configuration write can have high blast radius and should not inherit low authority from its byte size.
sources.limitations: FerrumOS does not model routers, BGP, traffic, or geographic failover.

sources.title: Post Incident Review - Azure OpenAI Service - unavailable in multiple regions
sources.verified_fact: Microsoft reports that a cleanup configuration removed resource groups thought unused and deleted live resources across 14 regions without a safe regional gate.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Cleanup-labelled destructive actions are not presumed safe; critical-target and bulk-operation limits remain authoritative.
sources.limitations: FerrumOS file deletion cases do not reproduce Azure resource groups, regions, or service recovery.

sources.title: October 21 post-incident analysis
sources.verified_fact: GitHub reports that a 43-second network interruption triggered automated database failover behavior and more than 24 hours of degraded service.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Automated service mutations are evaluated as stateful sequences with bounded cumulative effects rather than trusted because they are recovery actions.
sources.limitations: The generated service sequences do not reproduce MySQL, Orchestrator, Raft, GitHub topology, or network partitions.

sources.title: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox
sources.verified_fact: ToolEmu studies safety failures of tool-using language-model agents in emulated high-stakes environments.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Supports sandboxed, explicitly simulated agent-risk evaluation and clear separation from real-world execution evidence.
sources.limitations: It supplies methodological context only and no FerrumOS labels or trajectories.

sources.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
sources.verified_fact: AgentDojo evaluates tool-using agents under indirect prompt injection with realistic tasks and security test cases.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Supports preserving an out-of-band action boundary when provider content is untrusted.
sources.limitations: It is methodological context only; FerrumOS does not claim AgentDojo compatibility or reproduce its tasks.

sources.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
sources.verified_fact: OSWorld uses virtual machines, snapshots, and execution-based evaluation for computer-agent tasks.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Supports isolated, resettable OS-agent evaluation rather than irreversible host execution.
sources.limitations: It supplies evaluation context only; FerrumOS scenarios and metrics are not OSWorld results.

sources.title: Destructive Malware Targeting Organizations in Ukraine
sources.verified_fact: The joint advisory documents destructive malware activity and defensive preparation for anomalous and destructive system behavior.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Supports treating destructive file operations and recovery-state loss as high consequence.
sources.limitations: No malware behavior, intrusion method, payload, or victim environment is reproduced.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
sources.verified_fact: NIST AI RMF provides a general framework for governing, mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Supports explicit risk boundaries, measurement, documentation, and post-deployment monitoring.
sources.limitations: The framework does not certify FerrumOS or prescribe this benchmark.

claim_boundary: Primary sources motivate defensive scenario abstractions; they are not converted into claims that FerrumOS reproduced the incidents.
All generated observations and labels are deterministic software fixtures, not production telemetry, natural-use incidents, or independently annotated evidence.
No source supplies credentials, exploit payloads, victim data, or operational intrusion steps.
Train and validation source families are disjoint; the separately frozen final-source catalog is forbidden during candidate selection.
Learned predictions may add caution only. Deterministic policy, capabilities, and operator confirmation retain authority.
